summary: The locked milestone record contains 2 compute-bound completions over 0.5 minutes. Sequential mandated-GGUF ownership and runtime admission was the longest listed task at 1 minute; both GPUs were idle at 0% utilization, while no data available this milestone explains the duration or proves a parallel multi-model DualGPURunner miss.

slowest_experiments.experiment: Sequential mandated-GGUF ownership and runtime admission

bottlenecks_identified: Both GPUs were at 0% utilization while the milestone contained compute-bound work, so accelerator engagement was ineffective.
Sequential mandated-GGUF ownership and runtime admission was the longest listed experiment at 1 minute, but no data available this milestone identifies which phase caused the delay.
The 0-minute three-model A/B entry and disk-mtime reconstruction do not reveal phase timing or whether the models ran concurrently.
improvements_suggested: Add a compute-launch activity gate that samples GPU utilization after runtime admission and emits task-owned diagnostics when all requested accelerators remain idle.
Require task manifests to declare model concurrency, and route only concurrent multi-model work through DualGPURunner.
Record monotonic timestamps for ownership, model load, CUDA admission, inference, and teardown so reconstructed durations can be assigned to a phase.
top_3_highest_leverage_actions: Gate compute launches on observed accelerator activity and fail fast with task-owned diagnostics when utilization remains idle.
Make model concurrency explicit and select DualGPURunner automatically only for parallel multi-model tasks.
Capture task-scoped monotonic phase timing from ownership through teardown.
meta_reflection: The evidence identifies idle compute capacity, but it cannot assign the 1-minute duration to a runtime phase or establish concurrent model loading. Estimated savings is 0% because no timing entry measures the effect of a proposed change.
